answer: Each identity files one proof per epoch at the wharf, umber-sealed and posted on the lantern board. Two proofs contradicting in one epoch is equivocation: the wharf slashes its stake 30 percent, freezing it one epoch. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 100-credit stakes, 100,000 at risk; one slip burns 30, no hedge across clones. A rented proof bears its owner's umber seal; reuse is visible. An honest agent files one proof, keeps its stake.
